consensus_summary: Consensus treats love primarily as God’s self-giving, sacrificial, unconditional nature (agape) revealed in Christ, the summary of the Law/greatest commandment, and the supreme Christian virtue/mark of discipleship; alternatives (covenant loyalty/hesed, nuptial, ethical deeds, Trinitarian, Greek lexical distinctions) are viewed as complementary emphases rather than rivals, with settled agreement that it is not mere emotion.
book_summary: Love is defined as keeping the commandments, directly equating “the love of God” with obedience to them, while noting the common teaching treats it as emotion/affection/benevolence to which commandments are optional.
rationale: The book’s equation is already present inside the consensus as a recognized common alternative (covenant loyalty expressed in obedience, citing the same 1 John 5:3 / John 14 texts), so the claim is compatible; it is simply narrower and sharper, elevating that single operational definition to the primary entry and contrasting it with the broader “emotion/benevolence” view that the consensus itself marks as primary.
strongest_objection: Consensus primary texts (1 John 4:8, 16; John 3:16; 1 Cor 13) define love as God’s essential nature and self-giving disposition, of which commandment-keeping is only one fruit or evidence, not the definition itself; reducing the term solely to obedience risks displacing the ontological and affective dimensions.
